summary: DAY adversarial review independently challenged every company in the 12-name active batch against concentration, dilution/financing, accounting normalization, governance, substitution, regulation, execution and narrative-overreach. Cumulative primary evidence remains valid and fresh September signals were tested as potential overstatement vectors. No current evidence creates a lane-specific methodology blocker for any of the 12; all are ready_for_chief in this lane with explicit present risks and falsifiers.

companies.redTeamCase: The increasingly impressive partner list can create false confidence: Meta capacity, NVIDIA investment and Palantir distribution all depend on massive infrastructure execution. Strategic validation does not prove utilization, gross margin or ROIC. Counterparty concentration and funding intensity remain the dominant failure path.
falsifiers: material delay or cancellation of committed capacity
capex grows materially faster than contracted gross profit and operating cash generation
financing terms deteriorate as buildout expands
partner-channel announcements fail to convert into diversified paying demand

companies.redTeamCase: RPO and recurring imagery demand can hide capital intensity, government timing and constellation-refresh economics. Liquidity reduces immediate survival risk but does not neutralize dilution or replacement-capex risk.
falsifiers: RPO conversion weakens materially
satellite replacement capex rises faster than gross-profit growth
financing expands share count without corresponding cash-generation improvement

companies.redTeamCase: The biggest narrative trap is category leakage: an NRC isotope-material license for Atomic Alchemy is not an Aurora commercial-reactor license, and large framework agreements are not bankable generation revenue. Oklo remains dependent on licensing, fuel, project finance and contract conversion.
falsifiers: Aurora licensing milestones slip materially
framework counterparties fail to convert into binding economic agreements
project economics require structurally more capital or dilution than expected

companies.redTeamCase: The Malaysia AI offtake improves demand visibility but can be overread. More than $800M expected revenue is multi-year and starts in 2027; customer prepayments targeted at more than 50% of associated capex still leave material funding, execution, counterparty and margin risk. Mining beta remains economically relevant until AI cash flows actually dominate.
falsifiers: A102 energization or service commencement slips
offtake customers fail to perform or expected revenue/margins do not materialize
residual capex and financing requirements produce substantial dilution
self-mining capital needs continue to dominate cash use

companies.redTeamCase: Superion manufacturing milestones, updated guidance and the $8.18M quantum-security agreement are real evidence but are unusually easy to extrapolate into a fully validated quantum-computing business. SkyWater and prior acquisitions create integration/capital-allocation complexity; roadmap claims must not substitute for fault-tolerant commercial economics.
falsifiers: Superion deliveries slip materially or fail to generate repeatable commercial economics
post-acquisition burn remains high without margin progression
integration produces recurring restructuring/impairment or further large dilution
security/networking wins remain isolated rather than repeatable

companies.redTeamCase: Extreme customer concentration means backlog and deployment visibility can create false comfort. Walmart-linked deployment cadence, receivables and bargaining power should dominate concentration penalties until other customers become material.
falsifiers: principal-customer deployments pause or economics are renegotiated
customer concentration stays extreme while margins weaken
new customers fail to become material contributors

companies.redTeamCase: AI/custom-silicon enthusiasm can hide direct-customer, distributor and receivable concentration plus cyclicality/export exposure. Design wins should not receive full thesis credit until diversified revenue and cash conversion are visible.
falsifiers: major customer or distributor loss
custom-AI concentration rises while gross margin/cash conversion weakens
export controls materially shrink addressable demand

companies.redTeamCase: AI-optics growth is exposed to hyperscaler concentration, optical-cycle duration and leverage. Current pricing/yield gains may be cyclical rather than durable moat evidence; debt lowers tolerance for an abrupt demand reset.
falsifiers: AI datacenter growth decelerates sharply
top-customer concentration rises with inventory/receivable stress
deleveraging stalls during margin compression

companies.redTeamCase: Debt equitization improves leverage but the share issuance is economically real. Hyperscaler concentration plus 1.6T/CPO transitions create both upside and product-obsolescence risk; normalize per-share economics rather than celebrating only margin acceleration.
falsifiers: share-count growth remains material
CPO transition disintermediates current product economics
major-customer concentration rises while margins normalize downward

companies.redTeamCase: Strong margins and cash flow can hide channel/geographic concentration. Distributor receivables, Taiwan/China exposure and outsourced manufacturing remain dependencies rather than owned moat.
falsifiers: channel inventory correction causes disproportionate revenue decline
Taiwan/China disruption materially constrains supply or end demand
300mm expansion fails qualification or creates persistent cost drag

companies.redTeamCase: Rapid AI-infrastructure growth with high customer concentration creates peak-cycle risk. Revenue acceleration must be separated from margin durability, working-capital intensity and hyperscaler bargaining power.
falsifiers: top-customer growth reverses
working-capital/capex needs consume cash despite revenue growth
operating margin retraces as mix normalizes

companies.redTeamCase: Diversification is genuine, but the 2026 acquisition wave creates integration, debt, synergy and capital-allocation risk. Acquired growth should not be mistaken for organic moat expansion without realized returns.
falsifiers: integration costs or synergy realization miss materially
leverage remains elevated while organic growth slows
large acquisitions reduce return on invested capital

contradictions: Validated demand at NBIS and SYM can increase concentration and execution risk rather than reduce it.
BTDR's forward AI offtake materially improves demand visibility but does not yet establish realized economics or remove mining-cycle dependence.
IONQ's September milestones reduce specific technical/commercial uncertainties while increasing the temptation to over-capitalize roadmap claims.
OKLO's isotope-license progress is execution evidence in a related business but cannot be promoted into power-reactor licensing evidence.
APH diversification reduces customer risk while acquisition intensity raises balance-sheet and integration risk.
unknowns: Exact live crowding, short interest and consensus positioning are not canonical T0 underwriting inputs and are not fabricated.
Future regulatory, technology-transition and renewal outcomes remain falsifiers rather than present blockers unless sourced contradictions emerge.
peerRequests: Chief: all 12 active-batch names are red-team ready_for_chief, but readiness is not endorsement; preserve explicit concentration, capital-structure, integration and cycle penalties.
Underwriting: retain conservative treatment of OKLO framework economics, BTDR forward offtake economics and IONQ post-acquisition normalization.
Expectations-execution: treat NBIS/IONQ/OKLO/BTDR as highly narrative-sensitive and COHR/LITE/CLS/MRVL as AI-cycle-expectation sensitive without contaminating Earth Score.
